brief.headline: Energy leads risk-on tape; gold and tech diverge sharply
brief.regime_summary: SPY sits 1.4% below its 20DMA and 0.6% off last week, but remains 4.1% above the 200DMA and only 3% from its 1-year high. The label stays risk-on. VIX at 19.54 is elevated versus its 20DMA of 17.20, suggesting the market is hedging even as it holds the trend. Breadth is decent, with 7 of 11 sectors above their 50DMA. Sector rotation is notable: XLE, XLV and XLP lead on 20-day momentum while XLK is down 10.2% and XLC down 9.4%, a clear defensive tilt within an otherwise constructive regime. Tech weakness is not yet broad enough to flip the regime label, but it needs watching.

portfolio.note: Price at $521.91 is 1.7% below the 20DMA but 12.2% above the 100DMA; the MA stack remains bullish. RSI 49, momentum flat at +0.9% over 20 days. With XLK the weakest sector on 20-day momentum (-10.2%), the near-term path is choppy. Thesis intact: EPS and revenue revisions both positive, P/E 4% below historical median.

ASML is 6.9% below its 20DMA, 10% below the 100DMA, 16.2% from its 20-day high, and 20-day momentum is -16%. The MA stack is fully bearish and it is lagging the market by 14.2% over 20 days. Despite rising EPS and revenue revisions, the technical deterioration is significant enough to revisit position sizing and stop logic.

XLE at $70.02 is virtually at its 20-day high (-0.2%) with RSI 67.9 and 20-day momentum of +11.5%, the strongest sector reading in the screen. Bullish MA stack across all timeframes. Cost basis is $88, so the position is underwater, but the technical setup is the strongest in the portfolio right now.

GLD fell 2.95% last week to $355.78, sitting 5.3% below its 20DMA with RSI at 30.3, near oversold. The underlying gold futures show the same: 20-day momentum -5.7%, 40-day momentum -12.4%, fully bearish MA stack. Relative volume of 1.94 on the decline suggests selling pressure, not illiquidity. Watch for RSI to stabilize before assuming a floor.

watchlist.name: Accenture plc
watchlist.thesis: ACN gained 3.6% last week and sits 13.6% above its 20DMA at $258.24, just 0.8% off a 20-day high of $260.42. 20-day momentum is +30.9% and it leads its sector by 41 percentage points over 20 days. Revenue estimates are up 5.3% from the October baseline. Earnings are not until December 17, so there is runway for the technical move to continue if the tape holds.
watchlist.risk: RSI 70.6 is extended; a pullback toward the 20DMA would be a 13.6% draw, which is large relative to the ATR. Any deterioration in the IT services outlook breaks the thesis.

watchlist.name: Gilead Sciences, Inc.
watchlist.thesis: GILD surged 9.4% last week to $170.68 on a massive EPS estimate revision of +137.5% over 30 days (6 upgrades versus 1 downgrade). Price is 10.5% above the 20DMA with a clean bullish MA stack. Healthcare (XLV) is the second-strongest sector on 20-day momentum. Earnings were October 29, so the catalyst is likely already in the price.
watchlist.risk: RSI 74.4 is stretched; if the earnings revision surge was a one-time restatement item the fundamental case could unwind quickly.

watchlist.name: Chevron Corporation
watchlist.thesis: CVX at $235.52 is 6.2% above its 20DMA with RSI 72.9 and 20-day momentum of +14.0%. EPS estimates are up 8.2% and revenue estimates up 7.3% from the October baseline. P/E of 17.3x is 4.5% below its historical median. Energy sector leadership is the key regime tailwind this week.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: $221.76 (implied), 20-day high: $236.49 (implied from -0.4% gap), ATR-based stop distance: ~$4.57 (1 ATR, ~1.9%)
watchlist.risk: WTI pulled back 2% last week to $99.71; a sustained crude decline would remove the fundamental and sector tailwind simultaneously.

watchlist.name: ConocoPhillips
watchlist.thesis: COP reports earnings November 5. Price at $154.03 is 8.1% above its 20DMA, essentially at a 20-day high (-0.2%), RSI 74.4. 20-day momentum is +21.5% and it leads the market by 23.3 percentage points. EPS estimates are up 4% over 30 days. The setup reflects strong pre-earnings positioning in the leading sector.
watchlist.risk: P/E is 54% above historical median; any earnings miss or weak guidance, or a crude price drop into the print, could unwind the pre-earnings run sharply.

watchlist.name: Intel Corporation
watchlist.thesis: INTC fell 24.4% last week to $65.76 and is now 31.8% below its 20DMA and 44.4% from its 20-day high. RSI is 25.1, oversold but not yet basing. 20-day annualized volatility is 127%. EPS and revenue estimates are both being cut. Relative volume of 3.9x suggests the move is news-driven and distribution, not capitulation buying.
watchlist.risk: At this oversold level a short squeeze or positive surprise could cause a violent rebound; the ATR of $6.97 means daily swings of 10% are within the normal range.

watchlist.name: Caterpillar, Inc.
watchlist.thesis: CAT dropped 9.1% last week to $622.75 and sits 16.2% below its 20DMA and 28.8% from its 20-day high. RSI 23.97 is deeply oversold. Industrials (XLI) is the weakest non-tech sector. 20-day momentum is -26.2%, 40-day -22.0%. Despite a small EPS revision uptick, the price action suggests the market is pricing in a more significant fundamental shift.
watchlist.risk: RSI under 24 can snap back hard on any positive macro data (ISM, China stimulus); oversold does not mean bottomed in a bearish MA stack.

commodities.name: WTI Crude
commodities.note: WTI at $99.71 pulled back 2% last week but holds its 20DMA (+1.8%) with 20-day momentum of +11.5% and a bullish MA stack. RSI 53 is neutral, and the 20-day high gap of 9.8% leaves room for further retreat before the trend breaks. Watch the $96 area (20DMA) as the key support.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.note: Gold fell 2.9% last week to $3,921.50, now 4.4% below its 20DMA with RSI 30.7 approaching oversold and 20-day momentum -5.7%. The bearish MA stack and 40-day momentum of -12.4% suggest the correction is not finished; GLD portfolio position reflects the same deterioration.

commodities.name: Natural Gas
commodities.note: Natural gas jumped 13.4% last week to $2.95 but remains 1.5% below its 20DMA with 20-day momentum still negative at -3.8%. The spike looks seasonal or weather-driven; RSI 50 is neutral. High volatility (51%) and thin liquidity warrant caution on reading this as a durable trend change.

commodities.name: Silver
commodities.note: Silver fell 7% last week to $50.33 and is now 10.4% below its 20DMA with RSI 28.3 and 20-day momentum -17.3%. Relative volume of 18.7x is extreme and suggests a disorderly move. Watch gold for stabilization first before assessing silver's floor.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.note: Copper is flat on the week at $6.509, hovering just 0.8% below its 20DMA with RSI 47.5 and near-zero momentum. Relative volume of 5.8x is elevated for a flat price week, signaling positioning activity. Copper's directionless hold is worth monitoring as a macro growth proxy.

risks: COP earnings November 5: pre-earnings run of 21.5% over 20 days creates asymmetric downside risk if guidance disappoints.
INTC down 24% last week with estimates cut and 127% realized volatility; the stock is a source of sector-level contagion risk for XLK names.
VIX at 19.54 versus 20DMA of 17.20 signals the market is paying above-average insurance costs despite the risk-on label; a vol spike could hit extended RSI names (GILD 74, CVX 73, COP 74) hard.
Gold and silver in simultaneous oversold breakdown (RSI 30.7 and 28.3 respectively) may indicate broader safe-haven demand rotation out of real assets; monitor for spillover into risk sentiment.
XLK 20-day momentum of -10.2% with ASML and INTC both in steep downtrends creates drag on the portfolio's tech exposure; sector laggard status makes any broad rally in tech harder to count on.
